newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh filmed near where bombing truck rented.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh filmed near where bombing truck rented.

text.p: A former McDonald's restaurant manager on Friday identified Timothy McVeigh as a customer who bought an apple pie just minutes before the truck used in the Oklahoma City bombing was rented at a nearby shop.

McVeigh watched with interest as the manager played a security camera video of the Gulf War veteran entering a Junction City, Kansas, McDonald's and making a purchase. McVeigh stood up for the jury so the man could identify him.

It was the defence who asked McDonald's manager David D'Albini to identify McVeigh because it claims that a man dressed entirely differently from McVeigh rented the truck just 15 minutes after the accused Oklahoma City bomber was filmed at McDonald's.
The truck rental agency is about 1.5 miles (2.4 km) away from the McDonald's and can be reached on foot in about 15 minutes.

"It's him, isn't it?" McVeigh defence lawyer Stephen Jones asked D'Albini, who agreed. In the tape, McVeigh is shown wearing a dark civilian shirt and jeans. The tail of the shirt is sticking out of his pants.

The film was taken just before 4 p.m. on April 17, 1995, about 15 minutes before a man dressed in military style camouflage clothing walked into Elliott's Body Shop and rented the Ryder truck that prosecutors say was used to destroy the Alfred P. Murrah federal building two days later, killing 168 people.

The truck was rented to a "Robert Kling", a name prosecutors say was an alias concocted by McVeigh to rent the truck. A previous witness, Lori Fortier, the wife of McVeigh's army friend Michael Fortier, has testified that she helped forge a driver's license for McVeigh under that name.
The prosecution spent much of Friday tying McVeigh to being near the rental agency and to the name Robert Kling.
Friday's first witness was the owner of a Chinese restaurant who testified that she took a food order over the phone from a "Mr Kling".
Yuhua Bai, the owner of the Hunan Palace, said the caller placed an order for egg rolls and Moo Goo Gai Pan on April 15, and that she noticed the name "Kling" because it sounded like a Chinese name.

In damaging testimony, the owner said she sent a delivery man to the motel room where McVeigh had registered under his own name in Junction City on April 14, 1995, five days before the explosion. The prosecution contends that McVeigh rented the truck in that City and drove it full of explosives to Oklahoma City about five hours away.
Also appearing for the prosecution was Marife Nichols, the Philippines-born wife of McVeigh's alleged co-conspirator Terry Nichols, who will be tried separately later.
Both Nichols and McVeigh have pleaded not guilty and if, convicted, face the death penalty.

Marife Nichols testified that on Easter Sunday -- three days before the bombing and while the family was eating dinner -- her husband received a telephone call, left the house 15 minutes later and that she did not see him until the next morning.
Outside the court, her lawyer told reporters she stood by her husband even though she testified in a limited manner for the prosecution. McVeigh did not look at her while she spoke.

Prosecutors have presented more than 80 witnesses in the past two weeks who have either testified about McVeigh's anger at the government, his efforts to buy components to make the bomb, or the pre-paid telephone card he allegedly used when planning the bombing.
